maria_support: Hey @jake_devex @tanya_eng — escalated auth failure from a customer (INC-8421). They get intermittent 401s on POST /v1/chat. They can reproduce from their side but want minimal repro snippets to try (curl + py/js/go) and exact steps to collect a debug bundle / request-id. Can one of you paste tiny examples I can send back?

jake_devex: Sure — pasting the minimal curl + SDK examples. Note to customer: set REDWOOD_API_KEY and run curl with -i or -v to capture headers (we need the x-request-id). Also ask them to redact the API key before sharing any logs.

jake_devex: ```bash
# curl (include headers, show request/response)
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REPLACE_ME
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}], "model":"redwood-1"}'

# ask customer to copy the full response headers and body. x-request-id header is critical.
```

jake_devex: Python (requests) minimal:```python
import os
import requests

api_key = os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat"
payload = {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "model": "redwood-1"}
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))
print(resp.text)
```

jake_devex: Node (fetch) example:```js
// node >=18 or use node-fetch
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
const apiKey = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }], model: 'redwood-1' })
})
console.log(res.status)
console.log(res.headers.get('x-request-id'))
console.log(await res.text())
```

jake_devex: Go (net/http) tiny repro:```go
package main

import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)

func main() {
  apiKey := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  url := "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat"
  body := []byte(`{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"model":"redwood-1"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewBuffer(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { panic(err) }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  fmt.Println("status:", resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println("x-request-id:", resp.Header.Get("x-request-id"))
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

jake_devex: Also include these exact instructions for the customer to collect diagnostic traces:
- Run curl with `--trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt` or `-v` and upload the trace.
- Capture response headers (we need `x-request-id`) and exact server time.
- If using SDK, run the minimal snippet above and copy stdout (status + x-request-id + body).
- If they are on Linux/mac, run `env | grep -i redwood` and confirm the envvar is present (advise them to redact key before posting).

jake_devex: If they can run a debug bundle client-side:```bash
# internal helper we provide for customers (ask them to run and then upload)
redwoodctl collect-debug --output debug-bundle.tar.gz --include-trace /tmp/trace.txt --note "INC-8421"
# then upload the tarball to the support upload link we give them
```

tanya_eng: A few engineering notes to include to avoid noisy info:
- Ask customer to reproduce with a single request (no retries) so we get a clean x-request-id per attempt.
- If they see a 401, request the exact timestamp (with timezone) and the x-request-id header — that lets us pull server-side logs.
- If they cannot run `redwoodctl`, we can pull logs from the backend given the `x-request-id` + timestamp window (please provide range +/- 1 min).
- For curl traces, `--trace-ascii` is more useful than `-v` because it includes full request bytes.

tanya_eng: Quick snippet to show how to capture x-request-id with verbose curl:```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REPLACE_ME
curl -s -D /tmp/headers.txt -o /tmp/body.txt -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"model":"redwood-1"}'
# then
cat /tmp/headers.txt | grep -i x-request-id
cat /tmp/body.txt
```

debug-bot: If a debug bundle is generated and uploaded, reply here with the support-upload URL so SRE/Eng can fetch it. :robot_face:

maria_support: Perfect, thanks both. I'll send these instructions to the customer and ask them to return:
- the exact `x-request-id` header value(s),
- the curl trace or SDK stdout,
- a debug-bundle if they can run `redwoodctl` (or permission/time + timestamps so we can pull logs on our side).

maria_support: I'll follow up in this thread once they reply. :thumbsup:
